flags.name: api-version
flags.description: API generation v1 or v2; precedence: explicit flag > PLANE_CLI_API_VERSION > selected connection > v2 default

flags.name: name
flags.description: Return the type with this name, compared case-insensitively. `?name=bug` matches `Bug`.

flags.name: external-id
flags.description: Return types whose `external_id` matches exactly. Use it to find the type you created earlier for a record in another system.

flags.name: external-source
flags.description: Return types from one source system, for example `jira`. Combine it with `external_id`, because an `external_id` is unique only within its source.

flags.name: order-by
flags.description:
Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending.

- `level` , `-level`: the type hierarchy level
- `name` , `-name`: alphabetical
- `created_at` , `-created_at`: when each type was added
- `id` , `-id`

Order by `level` when you are rendering types to a user; it is the order the project itself uses.

flags.name: per-page
flags.description: Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most projects define a handful of types, so one page is usually the whole set.

flags.name: offset
flags.description: Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Use the `next` value from the response instead of computing offsets yourself.

flags.name: paginate
flags.description: Set to `cursor` to switch to the keyset envelope, which skips the `COUNT` query and returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Leave it out to get the default offset envelope.

flags.name: count
flags.description: Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT(*)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response.

flags.name: fields
flags.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Fields you don't request are left out of the response instead of coming back as `null`, so a missing key means you didn't ask for it and `null` means the value is null. `id` is always included, whether or not you name it.

Pass `all` to get every requestable field. An unknown field name returns `400` with the list of valid names and the closest match, so a typo is caught instead of being silently ignored.

Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `governance_mode`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_active_in_project`, `is_default`, `is_default_in_project`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`, `project_ids`, `rollout`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`.

See [Sparse fields](/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields).

flags.name: cursor
flags.description: Opaque next_cursor continuation documented by the list response.

summary: Get a work item type schema

flags.name: api-version
flags.description: API generation v1 or v2; precedence: explicit flag > PLANE_CLI_API_VERSION > selected connection > v2 default

flags.name: include
flags.description:
Comma-separated extra option lists to inline. Two values are recognized:

- `members`: inlines the project's active members as the options for `assignee_ids`, and for any custom property that is a user relation
- `labels`: inlines the project's labels as the options for `label_ids`

If you omit it, those fields still appear, but without an option list. These lists can be large in a big workspace, so ask for them only when you are rendering a picker, for example with `?include=members,labels`.

flags.name: include
flags.description: Comma-separated list of additional options to include: `members`, `labels`.

flags.name: id
flags.description: Work item type ID. If you omit it, the response contains the default type's schema when work item types are enabled, or only the standard fields otherwise.
